papers.title: Modulation and Power Losses of a Stacked Polyphase Bridge Converter

claims.statement: The inspected PDF is a different paper: “Communication-Based Distributed Control of the Stacked Polyphase Bridges Converter,” not the expected “Modulation and Power Losses of a Stacked Polyphase Bridge Converter.”
claims.source_title: Communication-Based Distributed Control of the Stacked Polyphase Bridges Converter
claims.supporting_excerpt: Communication-Based Distributed Control of the Stacked Polyphase Bridges Converter

claims.statement: The SPB converter consists of N series-connected submodules, each containing a conventional two-level, three-phase converter using low-voltage semiconductors; the AC terminals connect to a multistar load such as a multiphase machine.
claims.source_title: Communication-Based Distributed Control of the Stacked Polyphase Bridges Converter
claims.supporting_excerpt: It consists of N series-connected submodules, each comprising a conventional two-level, three-phase converter equipped with low-voltage semiconductors.

claims.statement: Each submodule has its own DC-link capacitor, and the total DC voltage is shared among the series-connected submodules; balanced operation uses a capacitor-voltage reference of vdc/N.
claims.source_title: Communication-Based Distributed Control of the Stacked Polyphase Bridges Converter
claims.supporting_excerpt: vref_conv can be chosen as vdc/N.

claims.statement: The converter control uses standard field-oriented current control in each submodule, with an outer DC-link voltage controller that adjusts submodule active power to balance capacitor voltages.
claims.source_title: Communication-Based Distributed Control of the Stacked Polyphase Bridges Converter
claims.supporting_excerpt: The outer voltage control balances the submodule active power; the inner current control controls active and reactive power in a decoupled way.

claims.statement: Phase-shifted carrier-based modulation is used so that the three carriers within each submodule are in phase, while carriers of different submodules are shifted by 2π/N; this supports cancellation of high-order DC-side current harmonics and reduction of DC-link capacitance.
claims.source_title: Communication-Based Distributed Control of the Stacked Polyphase Bridges Converter
claims.supporting_excerpt: The three carriers for each submodule should be in phase, while the carriers should be phase-shifted 2π/N rad among submodules.

claims.statement: The experimental prototype contains four identical submodules, each implemented on a single PCB with a DSP, isolated SPI communication, low-voltage MOSFET-based three-phase bridges, and local current and capacitor-voltage measurement.
claims.source_title: Communication-Based Distributed Control of the Stacked Polyphase Bridges Converter
claims.supporting_excerpt: Four submodules are connected... Each submodule is integrated on a single printed circuit board... Silicon MOSFETs are used as switches with 20 kHz switching frequency.

claims.statement: The prototype operating point used a 200 V DC supply, 50 V per-submodule capacitor voltage, 6 A tested AC peak current, 94 μF submodule capacitance, 20 kHz switching frequency, and 50 Hz fundamental frequency.
claims.source_title: Communication-Based Distributed Control of the Stacked Polyphase Bridges Converter
claims.supporting_excerpt: The main parameters of the setup are listed in Table I.

claims.statement: The experimental motor was a four-pole permanent-magnet-assisted synchronous reluctance machine with 12 available windings, allowing each of the four submodules to control an independent three-phase winding set.
claims.source_title: Communication-Based Distributed Control of the Stacked Polyphase Bridges Converter
claims.supporting_excerpt: Each of the four submodules is able to control a set of independent three-phase windings.

claims.statement: In the motor experiment, the four submodule currents had 30° electrical phase displacement due to the symmetrical winding arrangement; A1/A3 windings were in phase, as were A2/A4, while the two groups were shifted by 30 electrical degrees.
claims.source_title: Communication-Based Distributed Control of the Stacked Polyphase Bridges Converter
claims.supporting_excerpt: The current waveforms for the four boards have 30° electrical phase shift due to the symmetrical winding configuration.

claims.statement: A four-submodule experimental setup maintained DC-link stability for communication bandwidth below 1 Mb/s according to the paper’s Nyquist analysis and experimental verification, suggesting that CAN bus communication could be used.
claims.source_title: Communication-Based Distributed Control of the Stacked Polyphase Bridges Converter
claims.supporting_excerpt: System stability is still maintained when the communication bandwidth is lower than 1 Mb/s, indicating that the CAN bus could be adopted.

claims.statement: When one submodule was assumed faulty and bypassed, the remaining three submodules shared the DC bus voltage and total power; after a 50 ms transient, the system reached a new steady state and continued supplying the output power demand.
claims.source_title: Communication-Based Distributed Control of the Stacked Polyphase Bridges Converter
claims.supporting_excerpt: The remaining submodules share the dc bus voltage and the system enters a new steady state.

claims.statement: A single-submodule fault causes voltage rise in the remaining semiconductor devices, but the paper states that this normally does not destroy them because semiconductor devices are typically rated with a 50%–100% margin.
claims.source_title: Communication-Based Distributed Control of the Stacked Polyphase Bridges Converter
claims.supporting_excerpt: The voltage rise generally does not destroy the semiconductor devices since they are usually rated with a 50%–100% margin.

unresolved_questions: The supplied Jin2017.pdf does not contain the expected modulation-and-power-losses paper; semiconductor losses, machine losses, total efficiency, and power-density results for that expected paper could not be extracted.
The inspected PDF does not report semiconductor voltage/current ratings, converter rated power, efficiency, or power density for the expected citation.

papers.title: Comparative Evaluation of Three-Phase Three-Level Flying Capacitor and Stacked Polyphase Bridge GaN Inverter Systems for Integrated Motor Drives

claims.statement: The paper compares a three-phase three-level flying-capacitor converter (3L-FCC) with a stacked polyphase bridge implemented as two series-stacked two-level three-phase converters (2L-SSC) for a 7.5 kW integrated PMSM drive.
claims.source_title: Comparative Evaluation of Three-Phase Three-Level Flying Capacitor and Stacked Polyphase Bridge GaN Inverter Systems for Integrated Motor Drives
claims.supporting_excerpt: a converter system formed by two Series-Stacked Two-Level three-phase Converters (2L-SSC)

claims.statement: The 3L-FCC uses one flying-capacitor phase leg per phase, with four switches per leg and a flying capacitor; the 2L-SSC uses two standard three-phase two-level inverter stages connected in series on the DC side.
claims.source_title: Comparative Evaluation of Three-Phase Three-Level Flying Capacitor and Stacked Polyphase Bridge GaN Inverter Systems for Integrated Motor Drives
claims.supporting_excerpt: The 3L-FCC ... utilizes two half-bridge cells per phase (i.e., four switches in total)

claims.statement: The 2L-SSC requires a motor with two three-phase winding systems, with one winding set supplied by each inverter; one winding system is connected with reversed winding direction so that complementary phase currents produce torque in the same direction.
claims.source_title: Comparative Evaluation of Three-Phase Three-Level Flying Capacitor and Stacked Polyphase Bridge GaN Inverter Systems for Integrated Motor Drives
claims.supporting_excerpt: the 2L-SSC ... supplying a dual-winding-set PMSM

claims.statement: Both designs target an 800 V DC link, 7.5 kW nominal output power, 15 A nominal peak phase current, 45 A overload peak phase current for 3 s, 35 kHz device switching frequency, and 300 Hz maximum inverter output frequency.
claims.source_title: Comparative Evaluation of Three-Phase Three-Level Flying Capacitor and Stacked Polyphase Bridge GaN Inverter Systems for Integrated Motor Drives
claims.supporting_excerpt: Specifications of the analyzed Integrated Motor Drive (IMD)

claims.statement: Each semiconductor in both topologies is designed for a nominal 400 V blocking voltage, equal to half of the 800 V DC link; 650 V GaN devices are selected to accommodate switching overshoots and capacitor/DC-link ripple.
claims.source_title: Comparative Evaluation of Three-Phase Three-Level Flying Capacitor and Stacked Polyphase Bridge GaN Inverter Systems for Integrated Motor Drives
claims.supporting_excerpt: The required blocking capabilities Vds,nom = 400 V ... are identical

claims.statement: The selected power switch implementation uses two parallel top-cooled 650 V GaN HEMTs (GS66516-T, 25 mΩ) per switch position for both converter topologies.
claims.source_title: Comparative Evaluation of Three-Phase Three-Level Flying Capacitor and Stacked Polyphase Bridge GaN Inverter Systems for Integrated Motor Drives
numerical_values: 2 parallel top-cooled HEMTs per switch position
claims.supporting_excerpt: a single switch with two parallel top-cooled 650 V GaN HEMTs

claims.statement: The 3L-FCC has an effective switch-node frequency of twice the device switching frequency, feff = 2fsw; the comparison retains identical device switching frequencies for both topologies.
claims.source_title: Comparative Evaluation of Three-Phase Three-Level Flying Capacitor and Stacked Polyphase Bridge GaN Inverter Systems for Integrated Motor Drives
claims.supporting_excerpt: The effective frequency ... is twice the device switching frequency

claims.statement: Phase-shifted PWM is used for the 3L-FCC; its flying-capacitor voltage is ideally naturally balanced, but the authors state that active balancing may be required under practical nonidealities.
claims.source_title: Comparative Evaluation of Three-Phase Three-Level Flying Capacitor and Stacked Polyphase Bridge GaN Inverter Systems for Integrated Motor Drives
claims.supporting_excerpt: natural balancing might not suffice ... active balancing concepts ... must be implemented

claims.statement: The 2L-SSC requires a balanced DC-link midpoint; common-duty-ratio control is asymptotically stable for initial offsets and DC-link steps, but machine asymmetries of 1–2% can cause a steady-state midpoint offset and motivate active balancing.
claims.source_title: Comparative Evaluation of Three-Phase Three-Level Flying Capacitor and Stacked Polyphase Bridge GaN Inverter Systems for Integrated Motor Drives
claims.supporting_excerpt: in the case of slightly asymmetric machine parameters ... the steady-state DC-link voltage will have an offset

claims.statement: With complementary switching patterns and opposite phase-current directions, the 2L-SSC can ideally cancel its total common-mode voltage; the motor must use a reversed winding direction for one winding set to preserve torque direction.
claims.source_title: Comparative Evaluation of Three-Phase Three-Level Flying Capacitor and Stacked Polyphase Bridge GaN Inverter Systems for Integrated Motor Drives
claims.supporting_excerpt: in order to achieve mutual CM cancellation ... vCM,A(t) = −vCM,B(t)

claims.statement: For the 800 V, 35 kHz analytical comparison, a conventional 3L-FCC produces lower CM RMS voltage than a conventional two-level inverter, while the 2L-SSC approaches zero under ideal cancellation; a 100 ns relative gate-signal delay or balancing correction factor mf = 0.1 produces nonzero residual CM voltage.
claims.source_title: Comparative Evaluation of Three-Phase Three-Level Flying Capacitor and Stacked Polyphase Bridge GaN Inverter Systems for Integrated Motor Drives
claims.supporting_excerpt: the resulting CM voltage of the 2L-SSC is considerably lower than for the 3L-FCC

claims.statement: The modeled motor common-mode impedance is capacitive around the relevant switching frequencies and is represented by CCM = 4.4 nF, based on impedance measurements of a configurable multi-winding PMSM.
claims.source_title: Comparative Evaluation of Three-Phase Three-Level Flying Capacitor and Stacked Polyphase Bridge GaN Inverter Systems for Integrated Motor Drives
claims.supporting_excerpt: the machine behaves purely capacitive ... and ... can be modeled ... with CCM = 4.4 nF

claims.statement: The CM-choke designs use nanocrystalline VITROPERM 500 cores; the 3L-FCC choke has three stacked cores with three 19-turn windings and LCMC(70 kHz) = 13 mH, whereas the 2L-SSC choke has one core with six 6-turn windings and LCMC(35 kHz) = 1.6 mH.
claims.source_title: Comparative Evaluation of Three-Phase Three-Level Flying Capacitor and Stacked Polyphase Bridge GaN Inverter Systems for Integrated Motor Drives
claims.supporting_excerpt: CM Choke 3L-FCC ... 3× 19 turns ... CM Choke 2L-SSC ... 6× 6 turns

claims.statement: The 3L-FCC design requires one flying capacitor per phase; the selected implementation uses 24 parallel 2.2 µF, 450 V ceramic capacitors per phase, yielding 11 µF per phase.
claims.source_title: Comparative Evaluation of Three-Phase Three-Level Flying Capacitor and Stacked Polyphase Bridge GaN Inverter Systems for Integrated Motor Drives
claims.supporting_excerpt: a minimum of 24 paralleled ceramic capacitors for the FC stage per phase

claims.statement: The calculated nominal efficiencies are 99.05% for the 3L-FCC and 99.2% for the 2L-SSC at a baseplate temperature of 100 °C, with nominal operation defined at 15 A peak current, 330 V phase-voltage amplitude, and 300 Hz output frequency.
claims.source_title: Comparative Evaluation of Three-Phase Three-Level Flying Capacitor and Stacked Polyphase Bridge GaN Inverter Systems for Integrated Motor Drives
claims.supporting_excerpt: an expected efficiency of 99.05% for the 3L-FCC and ... 99.2% for the 2L-SSC

claims.statement: At nominal operation, the semiconductor losses are calculated to be identical for both topologies; the total nominal losses are 71.4 W for the comparison, and the 2L-SSC has lower total losses because its CM choke requires less impedance and winding copper.
claims.source_title: Comparative Evaluation of Three-Phase Three-Level Flying Capacitor and Stacked Polyphase Bridge GaN Inverter Systems for Integrated Motor Drives
numerical_values: Identical semiconductor losses under equal fsw
claims.supporting_excerpt: the semiconductor losses ... are identical for both topologies

claims.statement: For the CM-choke-based designs, the 2L-SSC is reported to require approximately 30% of the 3L-FCC CM-choke volume and nominal losses; the abstract alternatively expresses this as about 75% total volume and 85% nominal losses for the 2L-SSC relative to the 3L-FCC exemplary designs.
claims.source_title: Comparative Evaluation of Three-Phase Three-Level Flying Capacitor and Stacked Polyphase Bridge GaN Inverter Systems for Integrated Motor Drives
claims.supporting_excerpt: the resulting CM choke features only about 30% of the volume and 30% of the (nominal) losses

claims.statement: The 2L-SSC advantage depends on motor symmetry: with unequal winding-to-rotor capacitances, bearing voltage can occur even under ideal total CM cancellation; the paper calculates that approximately a 10% difference between the two winding capacitances is allowable for a 1.5 V EDM threshold under the stated model.
claims.source_title: Comparative Evaluation of Three-Phase Three-Level Flying Capacitor and Stacked Polyphase Bridge GaN Inverter Systems for Integrated Motor Drives
numerical_values: EDM threshold considered: 1.5 V bearing voltage
claims.supporting_excerpt: an approximately 10% difference between Cwr,A and Cwr,B is allowed

claims.statement: If a full sine-wave LC output filter is required, the 2L-SSC needs two filter sets for its two winding systems; the paper states that, for equal motor voltage quality, this causes twice the semiconductor switching losses and twice the filter volume and losses compared with the 3L-FCC.
claims.source_title: Comparative Evaluation of Three-Phase Three-Level Flying Capacitor and Stacked Polyphase Bridge GaN Inverter Systems for Integrated Motor Drives
numerical_values: 2L-SSC filter device switching frequency = 70 kHz in the illustrated comparison
claims.supporting_excerpt: twice the semiconductor switching losses and twice the filter volume and losses

claims.statement: The authors identify future experimental verification of the CM chokes for EDM mitigation as necessary; the presented CM-choke effectiveness is based on modeling, measured choke impedances, and circuit simulations rather than demonstrated bearing-current measurements.
claims.source_title: Comparative Evaluation of Three-Phase Three-Level Flying Capacitor and Stacked Polyphase Bridge GaN Inverter Systems for Integrated Motor Drives
claims.supporting_excerpt: Future experimental verification should confirm the effectiveness of the CM chokes for EDM mitigation

unresolved_questions: The paper’s principal comparison is design- and simulation-based; it does not report a complete hardware experimental validation of bearing-current/EDM mitigation.

The abstract’s total-volume and total-loss percentages refer to exemplary designs, while the conclusion’s approximately 30% figures refer specifically to CM-choke volume and nominal losses; these should not be conflated.
No direct measured drive-efficiency or motor-loss dataset is reported in the inspected body; the efficiency and loss breakdowns are calculated.
